definitions.explanation: A woman trained in the art of ninjutsu. In popular culture, depicted as a female spy or warrior who uses stealth and cunning.

examples.japanese: くノ{一|いち}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{登場|とうじょう}→登場：13625_toujou⟧⟦する→する：00392_suru⟧⟦{映画|えいが}→映画：02273_eiga⟧。
examples.english: A movie featuring a female ninja.

examples.japanese: くノ{一|いち}⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{変装|へんそう}→変装：12098_hensou⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{得意|とくい}→得意：03455_tokui⟧だった⟦と→と：00512_to⟧⟦{言|い}われている→言う：00515_iu⟧。
examples.english: It's said that female ninjas were skilled at disguise.

examples.japanese: マンガや⟦ゲーム→ゲーム：03842_geemu⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧、くノ{一|いち}⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{人気|にんき}→人気：01488_ninki⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦ある→ある：00006_aru⟧⟦キャラクター→キャラクター：23518_kyarakutaa⟧だ。
examples.english: In manga and games, female ninjas are popular characters.

notes:
ETYMOLOGY:
The word is a visual puzzle based on the kanji ⟦{女|おんな}→女：00559_onna⟧. When the strokes of ⟦{女|おんな}→女：00559_onna⟧ are separated, they can be read as く, ノ, and ⟦{一|いち}→一：00705_ichi⟧ — hence くノ{一|いち}.

CULTURAL NOTE:
Historically, female spies ({女忍者|おんなにんじゃ}) may have existed in feudal Japan, though historical evidence is scarce. The romanticized image of the くノ{一|いち} was largely created by 20th-century popular fiction, especially the novels of {山田風太郎|やまだふうたろう}. Today, くノ{一|いち} appears frequently in manga, anime, games, and period dramas.

WRITING:
Always written in mixed script: く (hiragana) + ノ (katakana) + ⟦{一|いち}→一：00705_ichi⟧ (kanji). This unusual mixed spelling is part of the word's identity.
